text: # Fraud and SIM-Swap Response Training **Document ID:** TRN_003 **Category:** GENERAL — Cross-Category / General **Department:** Security **Customer Scope:** all **Last Updated:** 2026-07-09 **Version:** 1.0 **Source Authority:** Internal Knowledge Base --- ## Learning Objectives - Understand the customer scenario this module covers and why it matters. - Apply the correct process steps consistently and within SLA. - Recognise when to escalate rather than continue troubleshooting. ## Core Content # Fraud and SIM-Swap Response Training **Document ID:** TRN_003 **Department:** Security **Category:** General (C01-C29) **Last Updated:** 2026-03-20 **Version:** 1.0 --- ## Learning Objectives Agents can recognise fraud indicators and execute the emergency SIM-block procedure without delay. ## Red Flags - Customer reports sudden loss of signal followed by unauthorised bank transactions - Request to change registered email/address immediately before a SIM swap request - Caller unable to answer standard security questions but pressuring for urgent action ## Immediate Action Protocol 1. Verify identity using alternate verification (not the compromised channel). 2. Block the SIM immediately if fraud is suspected — do not wait for full verification if there is clear and present risk. 3. Log as a P1 security incident per SOP_C18_FRAUD_RESPONSE. ## Assessment Agents are certified only after passing a simulated fraud-call assessment with zero critical errors. ## Key Definitions - **SLA** — the target time within which a request or issue should be resolved. - **Escalation** — handing a case to a specialist team when first-line steps do not resolve it. ## Worked Example During a routine interaction, the agent
